value.text:
More than eleven tackles a game, across 233 games.

Kyron Atwell has made 2,654 tackles in his career, about 11.4 a game, and picked off 39 passes, roughly one every six games. Among the league's own defensive backs only Damar Hobbs, Daren Teamer and Jayon Queen have more interceptions. There is no sack and no forced fumble on his line. He finds the ball carrier, he finds the ball, and he does both every week.

The road ran through Houston and Atlanta before the Jets secondary became his home in Y90, and his best work has come there. In Y92 he made 230 tackles and four interceptions in 17 appearances for a club that finished 6-11, the season that carried him over the line. He has a Defensive Player of the Year award and is still looking for his first ring.

He arrives in the Y92 class under the Career Legacy 7,500 standard. Kyron Atwell, welcome to the Hall of Fame.

value.text:
Twice in three seasons Ray Waller reached the Super Bowl and lost. Kyric McQuay was the reason both times.

Baby Manning did not beat you with arm strength. He beat you with decisions. In 10,099 pass attempts he threw only 43 interceptions, roughly one every 235 throws. He completed 6,048 passes for 53,797 yards and 562 touchdowns, and when the pocket broke down he could take it himself: 1,997 rushing yards and 107 rushing touchdowns.

He was Ray Waller's great rival through the Waller and Finney era, and twice his Colts met Waller on the biggest stage. Twice McQuay won, 38-32 in Super Bowl LXXXI and 29-28 in LXXXIII, the closest of finishes. Two rings, and two Super Bowl MVPs to go with them.

The best teams in this league rarely lost when it mattered. McQuay is one of the few who made them. Baby Manning, welcome to the Hall of Fame.

value.text:
Sixteen seasons in Dallas, and the Cowboys front had Keion Orzech in it for every one of them.

He came into the league in Y73 as Rookie of the Year and never left. In 271 games he made 1,296 tackles, close to five a game, with 13 sacks and 6 interceptions. The interceptions are the rare part. Defensive linemen are not supposed to catch the ball, and he picked off more passes than any of the great tacklers at his position. He reads the quarterback as well as the ball carrier.

There was no ring along the way and no Player of the Year award. There was a lineman who showed up for 271 games and stayed productive in all of them, which is its own kind of greatness.

He arrives in the Y88 class under the Career Legacy 7,500 standard. Keion Orzech, welcome to the Hall of Fame.

value.text:
Nearly three blocks a game. No lineman in the league has ever worked at that rate.

Akiem Brock came to the Eagles in Y88, the season Dorren Skura arrived in Philadelphia, and he has been on that line for all 100 games since. He has been credited with 293 blocks, 2.9 a game, well clear of Jawill Perkins, the next best at the position. Five seasons is a short road to the Hall. Brock made every one of them count.

The rings came fast. The Eagles beat the Broncos 40-22 in Super Bowl CXLVII in Y88 and beat the Bengals 44-14 a year later. A 32-22 loss to the Texans in Y90 was the only miss, and in Y91 Philadelphia was back on top, 38-23 over the Raiders in Super Bowl CL. In Y92 the Eagles beat the Colts 30-21 in Super Bowl CLI. Four rings, and like every lineman, no MVP or Player of the Year award to go with them.

He arrives in the Y91 class under the Career Legacy 7,500 standard. Akiem Brock, welcome to the Hall of Fame.

value.text:
Four Super Bowl rings on the Atlanta line.

Calais Ham arrived on the Falcons line in Y84. He has played 169 games and been credited with 331 blocks, close to two a game. Few linemen have done more with every snap.

The rings came one after another under Dorren Skura, in Y84, Y85, Y86 and Y87, the last of them at the end of a perfect 17-0 season and a 30-21 win in Super Bowl CXLVI. Ham was in front for all of it, without an MVP or a Player of the Year award, because linemen do not win those.

He arrives in the Y87 class under the Career Legacy 7,500 standard. Calais Ham, welcome to the Hall of Fame.

value.text:
Nine rings, and the best rushing seasons the record board has ever seen.

Ryland Maxwell came into the league with the Jets in Y80 and was Rookie of the Year, winning titles in Y80 and Y82. When Dorren Skura left for Atlanta after Y82, Maxwell went with him, and the Falcons won every season from Y83 through Y87. The Eagles traded Gerrit Ogbah for him before Y91, putting him back with Skura, and Philadelphia won Super Bowl CL and Super Bowl CLI.

In 245 games he has carried the ball 2,960 times for 23,556 yards and 329 touchdowns, and caught 159 passes for 1,169 yards and 51 more. He owns the single-game rushing record at 237 yards, the single-season touchdown record at 39 and the single-season yardage record at 2,670, set in Y87. Three Offensive Player of the Year awards and four Super Bowl MVPs say he saves his best for the biggest stage.

Ryland Maxwell, welcome to the Hall of Fame.

value.text:
Forty-three interceptions, and the league record now belongs to Damar Hobbs.

Hobbs has spent his whole career in the New England secondary, and in 265 games he has picked off 43 passes, one past Daren Teamer's old mark of 42. He has made 2,946 tackles as well, a little over eleven a game, so the ball hawk is also one of the surest tacklers at his position. There is not a sack or a forced fumble on his line. He plays the ball, and when the ball is caught he plays the man.

His ring came in Y81, when the Patriots got past the Packers 48-45 in Super Bowl CXL, a shootout that took 93 points to settle. There has been no individual award, only season after season of the same steady work.

He is still playing, and every interception now adds to the record. He arrives in the Y91 class under the Career Legacy 7,500 standard. Damar Hobbs, welcome to the Hall of Fame.
